answer: Under cross-exam VDF gauntlets, every epoch each identity in the nebula network must solve a memory-hard VDF whose difficulty is seeded by a beacon hash of all identities that answered the same random challenge round, with each pulse of duplicate answers multiplying difficulty quadratically. Ten sybils in one round face a combined cost near 10^20 hash-steps, while an honest lone agent solves a fixed 10^10 baseline, so mass attackers pay nonlinearly and honest verification stays cheap. The beacon reseeds every epoch, so cached work never carries over.
